newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain could outperform stability plan - Montoro.
newsitem.headline: Spain could outperform stability plan - Montoro.

text.p: Spain may outperform a new stability plan that some market participants have criticised as over-ambitious, Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said on Tuesday
The fiscal discipline plan, released on Sunday, sees economic growth at three percent or more through the year 2000, and a decline in overall debt during that period.
It also projects that the deficit will fall to 1.6 percent of gross domestic product in 2000 from a planned 3.0 percent this year.
Montoro brushed aside critics who have called the plan rosy, and too voluntary to ensure government adherence.
"We could manage a reduction to under 1.6 percent. We could do better," Montoro told journalists.
He added that the objectives would be reached with the same economic measures the conservative government has employed up to now -- austere budgets and economic liberalisation.
"We are applying the measures that we know how to apply. We are applying the measures we had planned to use," Montoro said.
